html:
Gukurahundi was the campaign of killing by the Zimbabwean army's Fifth Brigade in Matabeleland and the Midlands from 1983 to 1987, in which thousands of Ndebele civilians were killed.

The Fifth Brigade, trained by North Korea and loyal to Robert Mugabe, was sent in after attacks by armed dissidents, but it targeted villagers seen as supporters of Joshua Nkomo's ZAPU. Estimates of the dead commonly run to about 20,000. The name means the early rain that washes away the chaff.

It ended with the Unity Accord of December 1987, which merged ZAPU into Mugabe's ZANU-PF and made Zimbabwe in effect a one-party state. No one was ever tried, and the killings remain a deep grievance in Zimbabwe's south.
sum: Gukurahundi was the campaign of killing by the Zimbabwean army's Fifth Brigade in Matabeleland and the Midlands from 1983 to 1987, in which thousands of Ndebele civilians were killed.
